messages.content: I'm planning a trip to Munich and need to check the weather for this Sunday. Can you retrieve the weather forecast for Munich?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to fetch weather forecast for Munich for this Sunday. Use Open-Meteo API. We need latitude and longitude of Munich. Munich coordinates: approx 48.1351° N, 11.5820° E. So latitude=48.1351, longitude=11.5820. We want forecast for this Sunday. We need to get forecast for upcoming days. The Open-Meteo API can provide daily forecasts. We can request daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, etc. We need to specify timezone. Let's use "Europe/Berlin". We need to get forecast for next days. The API endpoint: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast. Query parameters: latitude, longitude, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,weathercode,timezone=Europe/Berlin. That will return daily arrays. Then we need to find the date that matches this Sunday. We need to compute today's date. Today is 2026-10-19. Sunday after that is 2026-10-21? Let's check: 2026-10-19 is a Thursday. So Sunday is 2026-10-22? Wait: 2026-10-19 Thursday, 20 Friday, 21 Saturday, 22 Sunday. Yes Sunday is 2026-10-22. So we need forecast for 2026-10-22. We'll retrieve daily forecast for next 7 days. Then parse the JSON and extract the entry for date 2026-10-22. Provide summary: max/min temp, precipitation, weather code description. We might need to map weathercode to description. Open-Meteo weather codes: 0 clear sky, 1 partly cloudy, 2 mostly cloudy, 3 overcast, 45 fog, 48 light drizzle, 51 light drizzle, 53 moderate drizzle, 55 heavy drizzle, 56 light freezing drizzle, 57 heavy freezing drizzle, 61 light rain, 63 moderate rain, 65 heavy rain, 66 light freezing rain, 67 heavy freezing rain, 71 light snow fall, 73 moderate snow fall, 75 heavy snow fall, 77 snow grains, 80 light rain showers, 81 moderate rain showers, 82 heavy rain showers, 85 light snow showers, 86 heavy snow showers, 95 thunderstorm, 96/99 thunderstorm with hail. We'll map accordingly.

We need to call the function.
